drugs.phenotype: Patients with the rs113993960 CTT/CTT genotype (do not have a copy of the CFTR F508del variant) and cystic fibrosis have an unknown likelihood of experiencing adverse events while being treated with ivacaftor/lumacaftor, as the frequency of adverse events may be influenced by the presence of other CFTR variants. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence the frequency of adverse events experienced during treatment with ivacaftor/lumacaftor.

Patients with cystic fibrosis and the rs113993960 CTT/CTT genotype (no copies of the CFTR F508del variant) have an unknown response to the combination drug ivacaftor/lumacaftor as this genotype is not an indication for ivacaftor/lumacaftor. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence response to ivacaftor/lumacaftor.

Patients with the CTT/CTT genotype (do not have a copy of the CFTR F508del variant) and cystic fibrosis may have decreased response when treated with ivacaftor/tezacaftor combination as compared to patients with the del/del genotype. This genotype is not an indication for use of the combination drug of ivacaftor/lumacaftor according to the FDA-approved drug label for this drug combination and response may depend on the presence of other CFTR variants. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence response to ivacaftor/tezacaftor.

Patients with cystic fibrosis and the rs113993960 CTT/CTT genotype may not respond to treatment with cavosonstat. However, conflicting evidence has been reported. Other clinical and genetic factors may also affect response to cavosonstat.

Patients with the rs113993960 CTT/CTT genotype and cystic fibrosis may not respond when treated with cysteamine as compared to patients with the CTT/del or del/del genotypes. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence the efficacy of cysteamine.

Patients with the rs113993960 CTT/CTT genotype (do not have a copy of the CFTR F508del variant) and cystic fibrosis have an unknown response to lumacaftor treatment, as response may depend on the presence of other CFTR variants. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence response to lumacaftor.

The current evidence base suggests that there is no significant association between the rs113993960 CTT/CTT genotype (no copies of the CFTR F508del variant) and response to ivacaftor. However, conflicting evidence has been reported. Indication of ivacaftor in cystic fibrosis patients with this genotype is dependent on the presence of other variants within the CFTR gene. FDA-approved drug labeling information and CPIC guidelines indicate use of ivacaftor in cystic fibrosis patients with at least one copy of a list of 33 CFTR genetic variants. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence response to ivacaftor.

Patients with the rs75527207 AA genotype (two copies of the CFTR G551D variant) and cystic fibrosis may respond to ivacaftor/tezacaftor treatment. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence response to ivacaftor/tezacaftor.

Patients with the rs77010898 AA genotype and cystic fibrosis may receive benefit when treated with ivacaftor and curcumin as compared to patients with the GG genotype. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence the efficacy of ivacaftor and curcumin.

Patients with the rs113993959 GG genotype and cystic fibrosis may not have improvement in chloride transport when treated with ataluren. Randomized clinical trials did not find improvement in chloride transport or improved pulmonary function after 2 rounds of 2 weeks of treatment. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence changes in chloride transport and improvement of pulmonary symptoms in patients with cystic fibrosis.

Patients with the rs121909019 GG genotype (do not have a copy of the CFTR R1066C variant) and cystic fibrosis may have decreased clinical benefit when treated with elexacaftor / tezacaftor / ivacaftor as compared to patients with the GT or TT genotype. Other genetic and clinical factors may also influence elexacaftor / tezacaftor / ivacaftor clinical benefit.

### Clinical Interpretation for rs113993960 in CFTR

#### 1. Clinical Significance
The variant rs113993960 in the CFTR gene is classified as **benign** by the ClinVar working group. This classification is based on a consensus statement from a working group, which suggests that the variant is not associated with cystic fibrosis (CF) or any other CFTR-related disorders.

#### 2. Disease Associations
There is no direct evidence linking rs113993960 to cystic fibrosis or any other CFTR-related diseases. The variant is categorized as an intronic variant, inframe deletion, inframe insertion, and coding sequence variant, but none of these types of variants have been consistently associated with disease in the literature or ClinVar database.

#### 3. Penetrance & Expressivity
Given the benign classification, the penetrance and expressivity of this variant are expected to be low. There is no evidence to suggest that this variant would lead to clinical manifestations of cystic fibrosis or other CFTR-related conditions.

#### 4. Clinical Management
Based on the benign classification, individuals carrying this variant do not require specific clinical management related to cystic fibrosis or other CFTR-related disorders. Routine clinical care and monitoring for other genetic conditions should be followed as per standard medical guidelines.

#### 5. Evidence Quality
The evidence supporting the benign classification of rs113993960 is derived from a consensus statement by a working group, which reviewed and classified the variant based on available evidence. While the consensus statement is a strong indicator, it is important to note that the classification is based on the absence of evidence for pathogenicity rather than direct evidence of benignity. ClinVar entries for pathogenic variants in the CFTR gene, such as NM_000492.4(CFTR):c.350_351delinsTT (p.Arg117Leu), NM_000492.4(CFTR):c.1777_1779delinsTAG (p.Lys593Ter), and NM_000492.4(CFTR):c.1075_1079delinsAAAAA (p.Gln359_Thr360delinsLysLys), provide strong evidence for the pathogenicity of other variants, further supporting the benign classification of rs113993960.

### Conclusion
The variant rs113993960 in the CFTR gene is classified as benign, and there is no evidence to suggest it is associated with cystic fibrosis or other CFTR-related disorders. Routine clinical care should be followed for individuals with this variant. The classification is based on a consensus statement from a working group and the absence of evidence for pathogenicity in the literature and ClinVar database.
